Obedience isn’t something we can simply demand from a child. It develops.

From “I can’t yet” to “I can sometimes” to “I choose to” - a child’s ability to follow a direction grows alongside their will and independence.

As adults, our role is not just to make children listen, but to create the conditions that help them develop self-discipline, choice and inner control.

Sometimes, before asking “Why won’t my child listen?”, we need to ask:
“Are they ready to?”

In Montessori, simplicity is intentional. It allows the child to focus, explore independently and engage deeply with their work. The classrooms are not meant to be overstimulating with bold colours, it is intentionally muted and as plain as possible- because sometimes, less around the child means more within the child!
